correctness.rationale: The proof gives an exhaustive symmetry decomposition with dimension counts, explicitly evaluates all eigenvalues at saturation, proves the sign inequality for every p,q>=2, and uses a saturated Fiedler test vector to show strict optimality when the positive eigenvalue dominates. Orbit averaging and nonnegative diagonal entries transfer the zero-holding conclusion to every unrestricted optimum; a convex mixture with I strictly improves both exceptional saturated points. The proof of the fixed-p expansion is an implicit root derivative. The accompanying verifier passed 5405 exact and numerical assertions, including full-matrix decompositions and exceptions. Finite checks are corroboration, not an infinite proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The old ordinary K_{p,q} optimal weight is min(1/q,2/(q+2p)) and its SLEM depends rationally on p,q. That formula cannot apply directly after inserting pq new vertices. Here two different original-to-middle edge probabilities and distinct 3x3/2x2 irreducible blocks are essential; the sign criterion 2(1/p+1/q)^2-(1/p+1/q)-1/p and its only two failures are additional statements. The known C8 cycle optimum subsumes only the excluded (2,2) special case; no novelty is claimed for it.

originality.rationale: Ten actual published-record and primary-web queries returned no same-object support theorem. The three inspected primary full-text materials address foundational convexity, unsubdivided K_{p,q}, cycles, Cartesian products, and distinct interlayer complete multipartite structures; the new graph has one private mediator per K_{p,q} edge and a genuinely two-orbit extremum. Nearby indexed findings about edge polytope spectra, fractional matching ellipsoids and complete-bipartite domination concern different invariants and do not imply the result. The current accessible prior claim ledger includes FMMC on coronas, split graphs and products, but none on incidence subdivision of K_{p,q}. Absence from search alone is not novelty proof; the assessment relies on direct statement/structure comparisons and retains specialized-coverage risk.
residual_risks: A specialized report on edge-incidence fastest mixing or subdivided complete bipartite networks absent from the searched index could already give the same support classification.

value.rationale: The natural operation of inserting one mediator for every edge of K_{p,q} creates a genuine incidence network with three vertex classes and two edge orbits. The theorem completely determines whether zero original-vertex holding is achievable at the global fastest-mixing optimum for all integer p,q>=2 and proves it holds for every optimum in the main range. It also gives an exact SLEM formula and a nontrivial imbalance asymptotic. Those are structural support and optimization facts with concrete interpretation in reversible averaging protocols, not an arbitrary small-graph computation.
